correctness.rationale: For d≥3, q_i≥2, at least one q_i≥3, the Alexander dual of the ordinary three-cut complex has faces whose every triple is connected. The actual proof classifies all maximal faces as coordinate-line simplices, coordinate-square tetrahedra, and long edges between words at Hamming distance ≥3. For a distance-two nonedge, exactly two common neighbors are the other corners of its unique coordinate square; distance≥3 cannot be extended by a third vertex. The square collapse removes an exclusive triangle and a distance-two diagonal, leaving a filled square, and coordinate-line simplices collapse to triangle fans; the residual Y is the standard two-dimensional Cartesian-product square/triangle cell complex. Coordinate swaps along filled squares and shortcuts within filled line triangles give simple connectivity of Y by canonical coordinate-normal-form loops. Euler χ(Y)=N−E+F+S and H2(Y)=Z^μ; Hurewicz/Whitehead then give Y≃ wedge^μ S². Adding the h long edges contributes h free circle summands. The integral Alexander duality index N−t−3 converts cohomology in degrees 2,1 to free cut homology Z^μ in degree N−5 and Z^h in degree N−4, no torsion. Nonzero μ and h imply pure Δ3 non-shellable. Independently checked E/F/S and distance≥3 edge counts for (2,2,2),(2,2,3),(2,3,3),(3,3,3),(2,3,4); for nonbinary cases (μ,h)=(6,12),(20,36),(53,108),(43,72). Finite checks corroborate, not replace, the all-parameter collapse proof.
residual_risks: Homotopy claim applies to Alexander dual, not Δ3 itself.
The infinite-family conclusion depends on the geometric coordinate-move and collapse argument; sampled finite ranks alone are not proof.
